Chapter 10: Redefining Strength and Moving Forward.
You know, strength is one of those words we hear all the time, but it’s so easy to misunderstand. Most people picture muscle, endurance, the ability to just power through pain.
But if you’re living with trauma, carrying shame, or just navigating the world in a body that’s often marginalized, real strength looks completely different. It’s quieter. It’s steady. Most of the time, nobody else even notices it.
Sometimes, strength is just getting out of bed when everything feels heavy. It’s finding the courage to speak up in a meeting, even if your voice is shaking. Or maybe it’s saying no to yet another diet, and yes to giving yourself another chance.
It’s about forgiving yourself—for the setbacks, for those moments of doubt, for not living up to some perfect standard.
Let me share a story. There was a father who spent years hiding his struggles, always trying to seem strong. One day, he decided to open up to his kids. He wanted them to see that real strength isn’t about never being hurt. It’s about healing. It’s about showing up, trying again, and loving yourself—even when it feels almost impossible. That honest conversation shifted everything. His family started to see him in a new light, and he began to see himself differently, too.
It really goes to show that strength isn’t one-size-fits-all. For some, it’s about surviving. For others, it’s about thriving. And honestly? Most of us are somewhere in between.
What truly matters is that you keep moving forward. Keep hoping. Keep believing that change is possible, even if it feels out of reach some days.
This journey—it’s ongoing. Sure, there will be setbacks and times when doubt creeps in, or the world just feels way too heavy.
But there will also be moments of joy, of real connection, and even peace.
Your body, with all its scars and stories, isn’t a problem that needs fixing. It’s a living record. A testament to survival, to resilience… and to hope.
